## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vātamigajātaka* (Ja 14) is a canonical birth story found in the first book (*Ekanipāta*) of the Pali Jātaka collection [Burlingame 1921]. According to the narrative framework of the commentary, the story of the present (*paccuppannavatthu*) was delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana concerning the Elder Tissa (Direct-alms the Less). Tissa, formerly a prince of Rājagaha who had joined the monastic order only after undertaking a seven-day fast modeled on Raṭṭhapāla's resolution to overcome his parents' refusal, became entangled once again through the allurements of food and taste [Burlingame 1921].

To illustrate the danger of sensory craving, the Buddha relates the story of the past (*atītavatthu*): in ancient Benares, a royal gardener named Sañjaya managed to trap a timid wild antelope (or deer) by systematically enticing it with grass coated in honey, ultimately luring the creature directly into the royal palace [Burlingame 1921; Anandajoti 2010]. The central canonical verse, recited on that occasion by the king's wise minister, warns that there is nothing more ruinous than the craving for flavors, which exceeds even attachments to home or companionship (*na kiratthi rasehi pāpiyo, āvāsehi va santhavehi vā*) [Burlingame 1921; Anandajoti 2010]. Moved by this reflection, the king releases the captured animal [Burlingame 1921]. In the concluding identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the entrapped antelope is identified with the monk bound by craving, while the wise minister who uttered the stanza was the Bodhisatta [Burlingame 1921]. The narrative also appears depicted in Tibetan Buddhist biographical and geographical painting, localized around Rājagṛha [Schwartzberg].

In algorithmic text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identified no internal Pali parallels and no cross-language matches above threshold [DharmaNexus].
